chunks: Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), Al-Qaswa, whenever he descended from it, he would hang its reins upon it. He said: So it would go out and come to the Muslims. He said: So a man would give it something, and another man would give it something, so it would not remain long before it was satisfied. He said: So it put its head into the tent of Samarah ibn Jundab, so he took a stick and struck it upon its head, so he scratched it. So it went out to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him.

key_terms.الْقَصْوَاءُ: Al-Qaswa, the specific name of the Prophet's she-camel
key_terms.سَمُرَةَ بْنِ جُنْدَبٍ: Samarah ibn Jundab, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet's camel Al-Qaswa entered Samarah ibn Jundab's tent?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique status of the Prophet’s camel, Al-Qaswa, which served as a means of sustenance for the community through its personified acceptance of offerings. The incident involving Samarah ibn Jundab, who struck the camel and injured it, is often cited by Shia scholars to illustrate the distinct spiritual and physical characteristics of the Prophet’s animals, with some traditions suggesting Al-Qaswa possessed the ability to understand human speech and respond to grievances.
